title.zh: 卷三十八 志第二十八 地理二
title.raw: 卷三十八 志第二十八 地理二 Volume 38 Treatises 32: Gepgraphy 2

sentences.zh: 河南道河南道，蓋古豫、兗、青、徐之域，漢河南、弘農、潁川、汝南、陳留、沛、泰山、濟陰、濟南、東萊、齊、山陽、東海、琅邪、北海、千乘、東郡，及梁、楚、魯、東平、城陽、淮陽、菑川、高密、泗水等國，暨平原、渤海、九江之境。

translations.literal: The Henan Circuit, the Henan Circuit — broadly the territory of ancient Yu, Yan, Qing, and Xu; the Han commanderies of Henan, Hongnong, Yingchuan, Runan, Chenliu, Pei, Taishan, Jiyin, Jinan, Donglai, Qi, Shanyang, Donghai, Langye, Beihai, Qiancheng, and Dongjun; and the kingdoms of Liang, Chu, Lu, Dongping, Chengyang, Huaiyang, Zichuan, Gaomi, and Sishui, together with the territories of Pingyuan, Bohai, and Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Henan Circuit broadly comprised the ancient domains of Yu, Yan, Qing, and Xu — encompassing the Han-era commanderies from Henan and Hongnong east through the Qi and Lu heartland, the feudatory kingdoms of Liang, Chu, Lu, and their neighbors, and the reaches of Pingyuan, Bohai, and Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 洛、陝負河而北，為實沈分；

translations.literal: Luoyang and Shan, north of the Yellow River, constituted the Shishen division.
translations.idiomatic: The lands north of the Yellow River around Luoyang and Shan fell within the Shishen astrological division.

sentences.zh: 負河而南，虢、汝、許及新鄭之地，為鶉火分；

translations.literal: South of the Yellow River — the territories of Guo, Ru, Xu, and Xinzheng — constituted the Chunhuo division.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yellow River, the regions of Guo, Ru, Xu, and Xinzheng belonged to the Chunhuo astrological division.

translations.literal: Zheng, Bian, Chen, Cai, and Ying constituted the Shouxing division.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng, Bian, Chen, Cai, and Ying fell within the Shouxing astrological division.

sentences.zh: 宋、亳、徐、宿、鄆、曹、濮為大火分；

translations.literal: Song, Bo, Xu, Su, Yun, Cao, and Pu constituted the Dahuo division.
translations.idiomatic: Song, Bo, Xu, Su, Yun, Cao, and Pu belonged to the Dahuo (Antares) astrological division.

translations.literal: Yan, Hai, Yi, and Si constituted the Jianglou division.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, Hai, Yi, and Si fell within the Jianglou astrological division.

sentences.zh: 青、淄、密、登、萊、齊、棣為玄枵分；

translations.literal: Qing, Zi, Mi, Deng, Lai, Qi, and Di constituted the Xuanxiao division.
translations.idiomatic: Qing, Zi, Mi, Deng, Lai, Qi, and Di belonged to the Xuanxiao astrological division.

translations.literal: Hua constituted the Juzi division.
translations.idiomatic: Hua fell within the Juzi astrological division.

translations.literal: Hao constituted the Xingji division.
translations.idiomatic: Hao belonged to the Xingji astrological division.

sentences.zh: 為府一，州二十九，縣百九十六。

translations.literal: There were one superior prefecture, twenty-nine prefectures, and one hundred ninety-six counties.
translations.idiomatic: The circuit comprised one superior prefecture, twenty-nine prefectures, and one hundred ninety-six counties.

sentences.zh: 其名山：三崤、少室、砥柱、蒙、嶧、嵩高、泰岳。

translations.literal: Its famous mountains: Sanxiao, Shaoshi, Dizhu, Meng, Yi, Songgao, and Taiyue.
translations.idiomatic: Its notable mountains were Sanxiao, Shaoshi, Dizhu, Meng, Yi, Songgao, and Taiyue.

sentences.zh: 其大川：伊、洛、汝、潁、沂、泗、淮、濟。

translations.literal: Its great rivers: the Yi, Luo, Ru, Ying, Yi, Si, Huai, and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Its major rivers were the Yi, Luo, Ru, Ying, Yi, Si, Huai, and Ji.

translations.literal: Its land tax: silk gauze, coarse silk, cotton, and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax was levied in silk gauze, coarse silk, cotton, and cloth.

sentences.zh: 厥貢：絲布、葛、席、埏埴盎缶。

translations.literal: Its tribute: silk cloth, kudzu, mats, and earthenware jars and pots.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute consisted of silk cloth, kudzu fiber, woven mats, and earthenware vessels.

sentences.zh: 都畿東都東都，隋置，武德四年廢。

translations.literal: Capital-vicinity seat: the Eastern Capital, the Eastern Capital — established under the Sui, abolished in the fourth year of Wude.
translations.idiomatic: The capital-vicinity seat was the Eastern Capital; established under the Sui, it was abolished in Wude year 4.

sentences.zh: 貞觀六年號洛陽宮，顯慶二年曰東都，光宅元年曰神都，神龍元年復曰東都，天寶元年曰東京，上元二年罷京，肅宗元年復為東都。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Zhenguan it was styled Luoyang Palace; in the second year of Xianqing it was called the Eastern Capital; in the first year of Guangzhai it was called the Divine Capital; in the first year of Shenlong it reverted to the Eastern Capital; in the first year of Tianbao it was called the Eastern Metropolis; in the second year of Shangyuan its status as a capital was removed; in the first year of Suzong it was again made the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: It was styled Luoyang Palace in Zhenguan 6, renamed the Eastern Capital in Xianqing 2, the Divine Capital in Guangzhai 1, restored to the Eastern Capital in Shenlong 1, styled the Eastern Metropolis in Tianbao 1, stripped of capital status in Shangyuan 2, and reinstated as the Eastern Capital in Suzong 1.

sentences.zh: 皇城長千八百一十七步，廣千三百七十八步，周四千九百三十步，其崇三丈七尺，曲折以象南宮垣，名曰太微城。

translations.literal: The Imperial City was 1,817 paces long and 1,378 paces wide, with a perimeter of 4,930 paces; its height was three zhang and seven chi; it wound angularly to resemble the Southern Palace ramparts, and was named Taewei City.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial City measured 1,817 by 1,378 paces, with a perimeter of 4,930 paces and walls three zhang seven chi high; its irregular outline evoked the Southern Palace enclosure, and it was called Taewei City.

sentences.zh: 宮城在皇城北，長千六百二十步，廣八百有五步，周四千九百二十一步，其崇四丈八尺，以象北辰藩衞，曰紫微城，武后號太初宮。

translations.literal: The Palace City lay north of the Imperial City, 1,620 paces long and 805 paces wide, with a perimeter of 4,921 paces; its height was four zhang eight chi; modeled on the Northern Asterism as a bulwark, it was called Ziwei City; Empress Wu styled it Taichu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Imperial City stood the Palace City, 1,620 by 805 paces, with a perimeter of 4,921 paces and walls four zhang eight chi high; conceived as an earthly counterpart to the Celestial Ramparts, it was named Ziwei City — a name Empress Wu rendered as Taichu Palace.

sentences.zh: 上陽宮在禁苑之東，東接皇城之西南隅，上元中置，高宗之季常居以聽政。

translations.literal: Shangyang Palace stood east of the Forbidden Park, abutting the southwestern corner of the Imperial City; established in the Shangyuan era, Gaozong in his late years often resided there to conduct governance.
translations.idiomatic: Shangyang Palace lay east of the imperial park, adjoining the southwestern corner of the Imperial City; founded during the Shangyuan period, Emperor Gaozong in his final years often held court there.

sentences.zh: 都城前直伊闕，後據邙山，左瀍右澗，洛水貫其中，以象河漢。

translations.literal: The capital faced Yique directly ahead, rested against Mount Mang, had the Chan on the left and the Jian on the right, and the Luo River ran through its center, emulating the Han River and the Milky Way.
translations.idiomatic: The capital looked straight upon Yique Gate, backed onto Mount Mang, was flanked by the Chan and Jian rivers, and had the Luo River flowing through its center — a layout evoking the Han River and the River of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 東西五千六百一十步，南北五千四百七十步，西連苑，北自東城而東二千五百四十步，周二萬五千五十步，其崇丈有八尺，武后號曰金城。

translations.literal: East to west it was 5,610 paces, north to south 5,470 paces; on the west it connected to the park; north from the eastern wall and then eastward 2,540 paces; perimeter 25,050 paces; height one zhang eight chi; Empress Wu styled it Jincheng.
translations.idiomatic: The outer enclosure measured 5,610 paces east to west and 5,470 north to south, joined the imperial park on the west, and extended 2,540 paces east from the northern stretch of the eastern wall; its perimeter was 25,050 paces, its walls one zhang eight chi high — a circuit Empress Wu named Jincheng, the Golden City.

sentences.zh: 河南府河南府河南郡，本洛州，開元元年為府。

translations.literal: Henan Superior Prefecture — Henan Superior Prefecture, Henan Commandery — originally Luozhou; in the first year of Kaiyuan it became a superior prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Henan Superior Prefecture (Henan Commandery) was formerly Luozhou and was elevated to a superior prefecture in Kaiyuan year 1.

sentences.zh: 土貢：文綾、繒、縠、絲葛、埏埴盎缶、苟𣏌、黃精、美果華、酸棗。

translations.literal: Local tribute: patterned damask, silk, fine silk, silk-kudzu, earthenware jars and pots, gouqi, huangjing, fine fruits and flowers, and sour jujubes.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included patterned damask, silk and fine silk, silk-kudzu cloth, earthenware vessels, gouqi berries, huangjing root, choice fruits and flowers, and sour jujubes.

sentences.zh: 戶十九萬四千七百四十六，口百一十八萬三千九十二。

translations.literal: Households: 194,746; persons: 1,183,092.
translations.idiomatic: It registered 194,746 households and a population of 1,183,092 persons.

translations.literal: Twenty counties.
translations.idiomatic: It comprised twenty counties.

sentences.zh: 有府三十九，曰武定、復梁、康城、柏林、巖邑、陽樊、王陽、永嘉、邵南、慕善、政教、鞏洛、伊陽、懷音、軹城、洛汭、郟鄏、伊川、洛泉、通谷、潁源、宜陽、金谷、王屋、成臯、夏邑、原邑、原城、鶴臺、函谷、千秋、同軌、餞濟、溫城、具茨、寶圖、鈞臺、承雲、軒轅。

translations.literal: There were thirty-nine garrisons, called Wuding, Fuliang, Kangcheng, Bolin, Yanyi, Yangfan, Wangyang, Yongjia, Shaonan, Mushan, Zhengjiao, Gongluo, Yiyang, Huaiyin, Zhicheng, Luorui, Jiajue, Yichuan, Luoquan, Tonggu, Yingyuan, Yiyang, Jingu, Wangwu, Chenggao, Xiayi, Yuanyi, Yuancheng, Hetai, Hangu, Qianqiu, Tonggui, Jianji, Wencheng, Juci, Baotu, Juntai, Chengyun, and Xuanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: It maintained thirty-nine garrison posts: Wuding, Fuliang, Kangcheng, Bolin, Yanyi, Yangfan, Wangyang, Yongjia, Shaonan, Mushan, Zhengjiao, Gongluo, Yiyang, Huaiyin, Zhicheng, Luorui, Jiajue, Yichuan, Luoquan, Tonggu, Yingyuan, Yiyang, Jingu, Wangwu, Chenggao, Xiayi, Yuanyi, Yuancheng, Hetai, Hangu, Qianqiu, Tonggui, Jianji, Wencheng, Juci, Baotu, Juntai, Chengyun, and Xuanyuan.

translations.literal: Henan: first-rank (red grade).
translations.idiomatic: Henan County was of first-rank (red grade).

sentences.zh: 垂拱四年析河南、洛陽置永昌縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Chuigong, Yongchang County was established by partitioning Henan and Luoyang counties.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuigong year 4, Yongchang County was carved out of Henan and Luoyang counties.

sentences.zh: 永昌元年更河南曰合宮。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchang, Henan was renamed Hegong.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchang year 1, Henan County was renamed Hegong.

translations.literal: In the second year of Chang'an, Yongchang was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Chang'an year 2, Yongchang County was abolished.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年復曰河南，二年又曰合宮，唐隆元年復故名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong it was again called Henan; in the second year it was again called Hegong; in the first year of Tanglong the original name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong year 1 it reverted to Henan; in Shenlong year 2 it was again renamed Hegong; in Tanglong year 1 the original name was restored.

sentences.zh: 有洛漕新潭，大足元年開，以置租船。

translations.literal: There was the Luocao Xintan; opened in the first year of Dazu to moor grain-transport boats.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Luocao Xintan (New Canal Basin), excavated in Dazu year 1 to berth grain tribute barges.

sentences.zh: 龍門山東抵天津，有伊水石堰，天寶十載，尹裴迥置。

translations.literal: East of Longmen Mountain reaching Tianjin, there was a stone weir on the Yi River; in the tenth year of Tianbao, Prefect Pei Jiong established it.
translations.idiomatic: East of Longmen Mountain at Tianjin stood a stone weir on the Yi River, built in Tianbao year 10 by Prefect Pei Jiong.

sentences.zh: 有瀍水，避武宗名曰吉水，宣宗立，復故名。

translations.literal: There was the Chan River; to avoid the taboo on Emperor Wuzong's name it was called Jishui; when Emperor Xuanzong acceded, the original name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The Chan River had been renamed Jishui to observe the taboo on Emperor Wuzong's name; when Emperor Xuanzong ascended the throne, the original name was restored.

translations.literal: Luoyang: first-rank (red grade).
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang County was of first-rank (red grade).

sentences.zh: 天授三年析洛陽、永昌置來庭縣，長安二年省。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianshou, Laiting County was established by partitioning Luoyang and Yongchang; in the second year of Chang'an it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianshou year 3, Laiting County was split off from Luoyang and Yongchang; it was abolished in Chang'an year 2.

sentences.zh: 神龍二年更洛陽曰永昌，唐隆元年復故名。

translations.literal: In the second year of Shenlong, Luoyang was renamed Yongchang; in the first year of Tanglong the original name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong year 2, Luoyang County was renamed Yongchang; in Tanglong year 1 the original name was restored.

translations.literal: Yanshi: capital-vicinity grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshi County was of capital-vicinity grade.

sentences.zh: 天寶七載，尹韋濟以北坡道迂，自縣東山下開新道通孝義橋。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Tianbao, Prefect Wei Ji, because the Beipo road was circuitous, opened a new road from beneath the eastern mountain of the county to reach Xiaoyi Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 7, Prefect Wei Ji opened a new route from the eastern foothills of the county to Xiaoyi Bridge, bypassing the winding Beipo road.

sentences.zh: 西北有故富平津、河陽故關。

translations.literal: To the northwest were the former Fuping Ford and the former Heyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Northwest lay the former Fuping Ford and the former Heyang Pass.

translations.literal: Gong: capital-vicinity grade.
translations.idiomatic: Gong County was of capital-vicinity grade.

translations.literal: There was the Luokou Granary.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Luokou Granary.

translations.literal: Goushi: second red grade.
translations.idiomatic: Goushi County was of second red grade.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十八年省，上元二年復置。

translations.literal: Abolished in the eighteenth year of Zhenguan; re-established in the second year of Shangyuan.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished in Zhenguan year 18 and re-established in Shangyuan year 2.

sentences.zh: 有恭陵，有和陵，在太平山，本懊來山，天祐元年更名。

translations.literal: There were Gong Mausoleum and He Mausoleum, on Mount Taiping — originally Mount Aolai, renamed in the first year of Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: It contained the Gong and He imperial tombs on Mount Taiping, formerly called Mount Aolai and renamed in Tianyou year 1.

translations.literal: To the southeast was the former Huanyuan Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Southeast lay the former Huanyuan Pass.

translations.literal: Yangcheng: capital-vicinity grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yangcheng County was of capital-vicinity grade.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，王世充偽令王雄來降，以陽城、嵩陽、陽翟置嵩州，又析三縣地置康城縣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Wude, Wang Xiong, a false appointee of Wang Shichong, came to surrender; Yangcheng, Songyang, and Yangdi were used to establish Song Prefecture, and land from the three counties was further partitioned to establish Kangcheng County.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 4, Wang Xiong, an official serving Wang Shichong's rebel regime, surrendered; Song Prefecture was established from Yangcheng, Songyang, and Yangdi counties, and Kangcheng County was carved out of their territories.

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan the prefecture was abolished and Kangcheng was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 3 the prefecture was abolished and Kangcheng County was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 萬歲登封元年將封嵩山，改陽城曰告成。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wansui Dengfeng, when intending to perform the feng sacrifice at Mount Song, Yangcheng was renamed Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Wansui Dengfeng year 1, as preparations were made to conduct the feng rite on Mount Song, Yangcheng was renamed Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年復故名，二年復為告成。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shenlong the original name was restored; in the second year it was again made Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong year 1 the original name was restored; in Shenlong year 2 it was again renamed Gaocheng.

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianyou it was renamed Yangyi.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianyou year 2 it was renamed Yangyi.

sentences.zh: 有測景臺，開元十一年，詔太史監南宮說刻石表焉。

translations.literal: There was the Solar Observation Platform; in the eleventh year of Kaiyuan, an edict ordered Nangong Shuo of the Directorate of Astronomy to inscribe a stone marker there.
translations.idiomatic: It had the Solar Observation Platform; in Kaiyuan year 11, the throne ordered Nangong Shuo of the Directorate of Astronomy to erect an inscribed stone marker there.

translations.literal: Dengfeng: capital-vicinity grade.
translations.idiomatic: Dengfeng County was of capital-vicinity grade.

sentences.zh: 本嵩陽，貞觀十七年省入陽城。

translations.literal: Originally Songyang; in the seventeenth year of Zhenguan it was abolished and merged into Yangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly Songyang, it was abolished and absorbed into Yangcheng in Zhenguan year 17.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年營奉天宮，分陽城、緱氏復置，二年省。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun the Fengtian Palace was built; it was re-established by partitioning Yangcheng and Goushi; in the second year it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchun year 1, with construction of Fengtian Palace underway, the county was re-established by partitioning Yangcheng and Goushi; it was abolished the following year.

translations.literal: Re-established in the first year of Guangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: It was re-established in Guangzhai year 1.

sentences.zh: 萬歲登封元年更名，神龍元年曰嵩陽，二年復曰登封。

translations.literal: Renamed in the first year of Wansui Dengfeng; in the first year of Shenlong it was called Songyang; in the second year it was again called Dengfeng.
translations.idiomatic: It was renamed in Wansui Dengfeng year 1; called Songyang in Shenlong year 1 and again Dengfeng in Shenlong year 2.

sentences.zh: 嵩山有中岳祠，有少室山；

translations.literal: Mount Song had the Shrine of the Central Peak; it had Mount Shaoshi.
translations.idiomatic: Mount Song housed the Shrine of the Central Peak and adjoined Mount Shaoshi.

translations.literal: There was Sanyang Palace, established in the third year of Shengli.
translations.idiomatic: It had Sanyang Palace, founded in Shengli year 3.

translations.literal: Luhun: capital-vicinity grade.
translations.idiomatic: Luhun County was of capital-vicinity grade.

translations.literal: There was Mount Minggao.
translations.idiomatic: It had Mount Minggao.

translations.literal: There was the former Han Pass.
translations.idiomatic: It had the former Han Pass.

translations.literal: Yique: capital-vicinity grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yique County was of capital-vicinity grade.

translations.literal: To the north was the former Yique Pass.
translations.idiomatic: To the north lay the former Yique Pass.

translations.literal: There was Mount Luhun, also called Mount Fang.
translations.idiomatic: It had Mount Luhun, also known as Mount Fang.

translations.literal: Xin'an: capital-vicinity grade.
translations.idiomatic: Xin'an County was of capital-vicinity grade.

sentences.zh: 義寧二年以縣置新安郡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yining, the county was used to establish Xin'an Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In Yining year 2, Xin'an Commandery was established with this county as its seat.

sentences.zh: 武德元年曰穀州，以熊州之澠池隸之，幷析置東垣縣。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude it was called Gu Prefecture; Mianchi from Xiong Prefecture was placed under its jurisdiction, and Dongyuan County was further established by partition.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 1 it became Gu Prefecture; Mianchi from Xiong Prefecture was placed under its jurisdiction, and Dongyuan County was carved out as well.

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Dongyuan was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 4, Dongyuan County was abolished.

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan it came to belong [to Henan Superior Prefecture].
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 1 it came under the jurisdiction of Henan Superior Prefecture.

translations.literal: There was Mount Changshi.
translations.idiomatic: It had Mount Changshi.

translations.literal: Mianchi: capital-vicinity grade.
translations.idiomatic: Mianchi County was of capital-vicinity grade.

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, Gu Prefecture moved its seat here.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 1, the seat of Gu Prefecture was moved here.

sentences.zh: 西五里有紫桂宮，儀鳳二年置。

translations.literal: Five li to the west was Zigui Palace, established in the second year of Yifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Five li west stood Zigui Palace, established in Yifeng year 2.

sentences.zh: 調露二年曰避暑宮，永淳元年曰芳桂宮，弘道元年廢。

translations.literal: In the second year of Diaolu it was called Bishu Palace; in the first year of Yongchun it was called Fanggui Palace; in the first year of Hongdao it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Renamed Bishu Palace in Diaolu year 2 and Fanggui Palace in Yongchun year 1, it was abolished in Hongdao year 1.

translations.literal: Fuchang: capital-vicinity grade.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchang County was of capital-vicinity grade.

translations.literal: Originally Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: It was formerly Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 義寧二年以宜陽、澠池、永寧置宜陽郡，武德元年曰熊州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yining, Yiyang, Mianchi, and Yongning were used to establish Yiyang Commandery; in the first year of Wude it was called Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Yining year 2, Yiyang Commandery was established from Yiyang, Mianchi, and Yongning; in Wude year 1 it became Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 二年更宜陽曰福昌，因隋宮為名。

translations.literal: In the second year, Yiyang was renamed Fuchang, taking its name from a Sui palace.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 2, Yiyang was renamed Fuchang after a Sui-era palace.

sentences.zh: 四年以洛州之壽安隸之。

sentences.zh: 東有神雀臺，天寶二年以赤雀見置。

translations.idiomatic: East of the county stood the Divine Sparrow Terrace, erected in Tianbao year 2 after a red sparrow was sighted.

sentences.zh: 本桃林，義寧元年隸虢郡，武德元年來屬。

translations.idiomatic: Formerly Taolin, it was placed under Guo Commandery in Yining year 1 and came under Shan Prefecture in Wude year 1.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年獲寶符于縣南古函谷關，因更名。

translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 1 a treasure talisman was found south of the county at the ancient Hangu Pass, and the county was renamed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 有浢津，義寧元年置關，貞觀元年廢關，置津。

translations.idiomatic: Du Ford had been a pass since Yining year 1; in Zhenguan year 1 the pass was abolished and a ferry crossing was established in its place.

translations.literal: There is Taoyuan Palace, established in the first year of Wude.
translations.idiomatic: It had Taoyuan Palace, founded in Wude year 1.

translations.literal: Xia: expectant grade.
translations.idiomatic: Xia County was of expectant grade.

translations.idiomatic: Originally under Yu Prefecture, it was reassigned to Jiang Prefecture in Zhenguan year 17, transferred here in Dazu year 1, soon returned to Jiang Prefecture, and was reassigned here again in Qianyuan year 3.

translations.literal: Ruicheng: expectant grade.
translations.idiomatic: Ruicheng County was of expectant grade.

translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 2, Rui Prefecture was created from Ruicheng, Hebei, and Yongle counties.

translations.idiomatic: Formerly Hebei County under Pu Prefecture, it was transferred here in Zhenguan year 1.

translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao year 1, Prefect Li Qiwu cut open the Three Gates to improve grain transport, recovered an ancient blade inscribed Pinglu in seal script, and the county was renamed accordingly.

sentences.zh: 三門西有鹽倉，東有集津倉。

translations.literal: West of the Three Gates is a Salt Granary; east is a Jijin Granary.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Three Gates stood a Salt Granary; to the east lay the Jijin Granary.

sentences.zh: 有瑟瑟穴，有銀穴三十四，銅穴四十八，在覆釜、三錐、五岡、分雲等山。

translations.idiomatic: The county held a Sesè Cave and, on Mount Fufu, Mount Sanzhui, Mount Wugang, Mount Fenyun, and neighboring peaks, thirty-four silver mines and forty-eight copper mines.

translations.idiomatic: Guo Prefecture, Hongnong Commandery, was a mighty prefecture.

translations.idiomatic: It was formerly Guo Commandery, with its seat at Lushi.

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan the seat was moved to Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: The administrative seat was moved to Hongnong in Zhenguan year 8.

translations.idiomatic: The commandery was renamed in Tianbao year 1.

translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included coarse silk gauze, tile inkstones, musk, digupi root, and pears.

sentences.zh: 戶二萬八千二百四十九，口八萬八千八百四十五。

translations.idiomatic: It registered 28,249 households and a population of 88,845 persons.

translations.idiomatic: It maintained four garrison posts: Dinghu, Quanjie, Jinming, and Kaifang.

translations.literal: Hongnong: closely-attached grade.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong County was of closely-attached grade.

sentences.zh: 本隋弘農郡，義寧元年曰鳳林，領弘農、閿鄉、湖城。

translations.idiomatic: Formerly the Sui Hongnong Commandery, it was styled Fenglin in Yining year 1 and governed Hongnong, Wenxiang, and Hucheng.

sentences.zh: 武德元年曰鼎州，因鼎湖為名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude it was called Ding Prefecture, named for Ding Lake.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 1 it became Ding Prefecture, named after Ding Lake.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年州廢，縣皆來屬。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan the prefecture was abolished, and all counties came under Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Prefecture was abolished in Zhenguan year 8, its counties were all reassigned to Guo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 神龍初避孝敬皇帝諱，曰恆農，開元十六年復故名。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, to avoid the taboo on the late Crown Prince Xiaojing, it was called Hengnong; in the sixteenth year of Kaiyuan the original name was restored.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Shenlong era it was renamed Hengnong to honor the taboo on the late Crown Prince Xiaojing; the original name was restored in Kaiyuan year 16.

sentences.zh: 南七里有渠，貞觀元年，令元伯武引水北流入城。

translations.idiomatic: The former Sui Shangyang Palace stood here, founded at the beginning of the Zhenguan era and abolished in Xianheng year 1.

translations.idiomatic: East of the county an old riverside road offered no wells for watering horses, and many beasts died of thirst; in Tianbao year 8, Post-station Commissioner and Censor-in-chief Song Hun cut a new route west from Chousang through Jinwang Slope.

translations.idiomatic: It had Mount Xiong'er;

translations.literal: Mount Fufu, also called Mount Jing.

translations.idiomatic: Zhuyang County was of upper grade.

translations.idiomatic: Assigned to Shang Prefecture in Longshuo year 1 and to Luo Prefecture in Wansui Tongtian year 2, it later came under this jurisdiction.

translations.idiomatic: South of the county lay Zhuyang Pass, abolished in Wude year 8.

translations.literal: Hua Prefecture — Hua Prefecture, Lingchang Commandery — expectant grade.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Prefecture, Lingchang Commandery, was of expectant grade.

translations.idiomatic: Formerly Dong Commandery, it was renamed in Tianbao year 1.

translations.literal: Local tribute: patterned damask, gauze, silk, sedge mats, and sour jujube kernels.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included patterned damask, gauze, silk, sedge mats, and sour jujube kernels.

sentences.zh: 戶七萬一千九百八十三，口四十二萬二千七百九。

translations.idiomatic: Renamed the Yicheng Army in Zhenyuan year 1, it received its present name in Guangqi year 2.

translations.idiomatic: Weinan County was of closely-attached grade.

translations.idiomatic: Weicheng County was of expectant grade.

translations.idiomatic: Zuocheng County was of closely-attached grade.

translations.idiomatic: Lingchang County.

translations.idiomatic: Pushe Reservoir owed its name to a grant from Emperor Xiaowen of the Later Wei to Vice Director Li Chong.

sentences.zh: 天寶六載更名廣仁池，禁漁採。

translations.idiomatic: Xingyang County was of upper grade.

sentences.zh: 天授二年析置武泰縣，隸洛州，尋省，更滎陽曰武泰。

translations.idiomatic: In Tianshou year 2 Wutai County was split off under Luo Prefecture, soon abolished, and Xingyang was renamed Wutai.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天元年復為滎陽，又別置武泰縣，二年省，更滎陽曰武泰。

sentences.zh: 武德四年，析州境置龍沮、曲陽、利城、厚丘、新樂五縣。

translations.literal: In Wude year 4 Longju, Quyang, Licheng, Houqiu, and Xinle five counties were split from the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 4 Longju, Quyang, Licheng, Houqiu, and Xinle five counties were split from the prefecture.

translations.literal: In year 6 Xinle was renamed Zhuqi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 6 Xinle was renamed Zhuqi.

sentences.zh: 八年，省龍沮、曲陽入朐山，利城、祝其入懷仁，厚丘入沭陽。

translations.literal: In year 8 Longju and Quyang were abolished and merged into Qushan; Licheng and Zhuqi into Huairen; Houqiu into Shuyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 8 Longju and Quyang were abolished and merged into Qushan; Licheng and Zhuqi into Huairen; Houqiu into Shuyang.

sentences.zh: 東二十里有永安堤，北接山，環城長十里，以捍海潮，開元十四年，刺史杜令昭築。

translations.literal: Twenty li east is Yong'an Dike, north joining the mountains and encircling the city for ten li to hold back sea tides; built in Kaiyuan year 14 by Prefect Du Lingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty li to the east lay Yong'an Dike, joining the mountains to the north and encircling the city for ten li to hold back sea tides; built in Kaiyuan year 14 by Prefect Du Lingzhao.

translations.literal: Donghai: upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Donghai County was of upper grade.

sentences.zh: 武德四年以縣置環州，幷置青山、石城、贛榆三縣。

translations.literal: In Wude year 4 the county was made Huan Prefecture, and Qingshan, Shicheng, and Ganyu three counties were also established.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 4 the county was made Huan Prefecture, and Qingshan, Shicheng, and Ganyu three counties were also established.

sentences.zh: 八年州廢，省青山、石城、贛榆，以東海來屬。

translations.literal: In year 8 the prefecture was abolished; Qingshan, Shicheng, and Ganyu were abolished and Donghai came here.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 8 the prefecture was abolished; Qingshan, Shicheng, and Ganyu were abolished and Donghai came here.

translations.literal: Shuyang: middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyang County was of middle grade.

sentences.zh: 總章元年隸泗州，咸亨五年復故。

translations.literal: In Zongzhang year 1 it was placed under Si Prefecture; in Xianheng year 5 the former status was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Zongzhang year 1 it was assigned to Si Prefecture; in Xianheng year 5 the former jurisdiction was restored.

translations.literal: Huairen.
translations.idiomatic: Huairen County.

translations.literal: Middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: It was of middle grade.

translations.literal: Yi Prefecture, Yi Prefecture Langye Commandery, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Prefecture, Langye Commandery, was of upper grade.

translations.literal: Local tribute: purple stone and stalactite.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included purple stone and stalactite.

sentences.zh: 戶三萬三千五百一十，口十九萬五千七百三十七。

translations.literal: Households 33,510, mouths 195,737.
translations.idiomatic: It registered 33,510 households and 195,737 persons.

translations.literal: Five counties.
translations.idiomatic: It administered five counties.

translations.literal: Linyi: upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi County was of upper grade.

sentences.zh: 武德四年析置蘭山、臨沭、昌樂三縣，六年皆省。

translations.literal: In Wude year 4 Lanshan, Linshu, and Changle three counties were split off; all were abolished in year 6.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 4 Lanshan, Linshu, and Changle three counties were split off; all were abolished in Wude year 6.

translations.literal: Fei: upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Fei County was of upper grade.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年省顓臾縣入焉。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan year 1 Zhuanxu County was abolished and merged into it.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 1 Zhuanxu County was abolished and merged into Fei.

translations.literal: Cheng: upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng County was of upper grade.

sentences.zh: 本蘭陵，武德四年以縣置鄫州，更名，別置蘭陵、鄫城二縣。

translations.literal: Originally Lanling; in Wude year 4 the county was made Zeng Prefecture and renamed, and Lanling and Zengcheng counties were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Lanling; in Wude year 4 the county was made Zeng Prefecture and renamed, and Lanling and Zengcheng counties were also established.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年州廢，省蘭陵、鄫城，以氶來屬。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan year 1 the prefecture was abolished; Lanling and Zengcheng were abolished and Cheng came here.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 1 the prefecture was abolished; Lanling and Zengcheng were abolished and Cheng came here.

translations.literal: There is iron.
translations.idiomatic: It had iron deposits.

sentences.zh: 有陂十三，畜水溉田，皆貞觀以來築。

translations.literal: There are thirteen barrages storing water to irrigate fields, all built since the Zhenguan era.
translations.idiomatic: It had thirteen barrages storing water to irrigate fields, all built since the Zhenguan era.

translations.literal: Yishui: upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Yishui County was of upper grade.

sentences.zh: 武德五年以沂水、新泰、莒置莒州。

translations.literal: In Wude year 5 Yishui, Xintai, and Ju were made Ju Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude year 5 Yishui, Xintai, and Ju were made into Ju Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年州廢，以莒棣密州，沂水、新泰來屬。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan year 8 the prefecture was abolished; Ju went to Mi Prefecture and Yishui and Xintai came here.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan year 8 the prefecture was abolished; Ju was assigned to Mi Prefecture and Yishui and Xintai came here.

translations.literal: There is copper.
translations.idiomatic: It had copper deposits.

translations.literal: There are Mount Yi and Mount Long.
translations.idiomatic: It had Mount Yi and Mount Long.

translations.literal: North is Muleng Pass.
translations.idiomatic: To the north lay Muleng Pass.

translations.literal: Xintai.
translations.idiomatic: Xintai County.

translations.literal: Upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: It was of upper grade.

translations.literal: There is Mount Meng.
translations.idiomatic: It had Mount Meng.

translations.literal: Mi Prefecture, Mi Prefecture Gaomi Commandery, upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Mi Prefecture, Gaomi Commandery, was of upper grade.

translations.literal: Local tribute: zi cloth, sea clams, and cattle gallstones.
translations.idiomatic: Local tribute included zi cloth, sea clams, and cattle gallstones.

sentences.zh: 戶二萬八千二百九十二，口十四萬六千五百二十四。

translations.literal: Households 28,292, mouths 146,524.
translations.idiomatic: It registered 28,292 households and 146,524 persons.

translations.literal: Four counties.
translations.idiomatic: It administered four counties.

translations.literal: Zhucheng: upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Zhucheng County was of upper grade.

translations.literal: There is salt.
translations.idiomatic: It had salt production.

translations.literal: Futang: upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Futang County was of upper grade.

sentences.zh: 本安丘，武德六年省郚城縣入焉。

translations.literal: Originally Anqiu; in Wude year 6 Yucheng County was abolished and merged into it.
translations.idiomatic: Originally Anqiu; in Wude year 6 Yucheng County was abolished and merged into it.

translations.literal: Renamed in Qianyuan year 2.
translations.idiomatic: It was renamed in Qianyuan year 2.

translations.literal: Gaomi: upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: Gaomi County was of upper grade.

sentences.zh: 武德三年置，六年省膠西縣入焉。

translations.literal: Established in Wude year 3; in year 6 Jiaoxi County was abolished and merged into it.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Wude year 3; in Wude year 6 Jiaoxi County was abolished and merged into it.

translations.literal: Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Ju County.

translations.literal: Upper grade.
translations.idiomatic: It was of upper grade.

translations.literal: There is salt.
translations.idiomatic: It had salt production.

translations.literal: At right: the Henan Surveillance Commissioner, seated at Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At right: the Henan Surveillance Commissioner, seated at Bian Prefecture.
